config.selectionRule: exact real-progress success -> exact score -> robust successes -> robust score

config.readoutSurgery: minimal regularized updates to existing decoder linear/residual output layers
config.selectionRule: A* preferred action first; sweep safe alternatives; the extension has a strict marginal blocked-action budget including terminal steps; score gains commit only when they satisfy the progress floor and quality budget; after a transaction rewind, a bounded temporary horizon regression is allowed so an earlier committed-prefix decision can be rewritten and rebuilt

interpretation: The full measured MaleCNS and V5 sensory/core policy remain frozen and active. Only the existing small motor readout output layers are minimally repaired. Terminal failures, long no-progress tails, and the first blocked action that exceeds the extension quality budget are all treated as repair frontiers. The marginal blocked budget is checked even when the same action terminates the episode. At each frontier the A* first action is preferred, but if that action is incompatible with the current closed-loop readout the script also evaluates every other immediately safe local action. For stalls, the earliest teacher disagreement in the current no-progress tail is repaired so the repeated blocked/waiting suffix is not protected. The update direction is projected into the exact nullspace of every earlier on-policy readout feature. Score-neutral or slightly score-negative tactical moves may be used only inside a bounded tentative bridge. If a tentative branch stalls and analysis exposes an earlier mistake inside the committed prefix, the transaction rewinds to the committed decoder and rewrites that earlier state. Immediately after such a rewind, the first rebuilt branch may temporarily end earlier than the committed rollout, up to --max-rewind-step-drop steps, because requiring instant recovery of the old horizon would make the rewind impossible. This exception applies only to tentative bridges after a rewind; permanent commits still require a real score gain with the configured progress and quality gates. The bridge commits only after later clean progress exceeds the last committed score; otherwise all tentative work is rolled back. Final success additionally requires the target horizon, the progress floor, bounded no-progress, the global blocked-rate gate, and the marginal extension budget.
